title: Solve Systems of Linear Equations using Matrices and Gaussian Elimination

children: Recall that a system of equations can be represented as an augmented matrix. The following elementary row operations can then be performed on the corresponding matrix.
Any two rows of a matrix can be interchanged.
Any row of a matrix can be multiplied by a nonzero constant.
Any row of a matrix can be changed by adding a nonzero constant multiple of another row to it.
A type 1 row operation corresponds to interchanging two equations of a system.
A type 2 row operation corresponds to multiplying both sides of an equation by a nonzero constant.
A type 3 row operation corresponds to adding a nonzero multiple of one equation to another.
Since these row operations transform the matrix into a row-equivalent form, none of these operations will change the solution of the given system.
A special kind of row-equivalent form of a matrix is called
A matrix is in row-echelon form if it has these three properties.
The first nonzero entry (leading entry) in each row is 1.
The leading 1 of a given row is to the right of the leading 1 of the row above it.
Any rows containing only 0's are at the bottom of the matrix.
